subject: Startups
title: Angel Investors vs. VCs
description: A 60-second lesson on Angel Investors vs. VCs.

hook.text: Before VCs write big checks, angel investors write small ones. Angels fund startups when no one else will.

buildup.text: Angels are wealthy individuals—often former founders—who invest $10K to $500K of their own personal money.

discovery.text: They invest earlier and take more risk. Many angels don't expect returns—they want to help and stay in the game.

twist.text: An angel who invested $500K in Uber's seed round saw a return over $25 million. The best bets are legendary.

climax.text: Angels fill the gap between friends-and-family money and institutional VC. Without them, many startups never launch.

punchline.text: Angels bet first, bet small, and sometimes win enormous.

quiz.question: How do angel investors differ from VCs?
options: They invest their own money at earlier stages
They only invest in public companies
